brief: October CPI (Tuesday, 8:30am ET) carries no year-over-year figure because last year's shutdown left no October 2025 base, so the market trades month-over-month core CPI alone. September's core printed hot at 0.33%, which drove rate-hike odds and bond yields higher. The Fed still held at 3.75%-4.00% on Oct 28 (10-2, Cook and Hammack dissenting for a hike), a week before midterms delivered a Blue Tsunami and the S&P's fourth straight weekly loss. Payrolls then beat sharply (165K versus a 70K estimate, unemployment down to 4.1%), pushing December hike odds to roughly 86% priced. Consensus expects core at 0.2% month over month, down from 0.33%. Goldman is the low forecast at 0.16% core, JPMorgan's Feroli the high at 0.23%, Deutsche Bank in between at 0.20%, on falling health insurance and used car prices plus flat airfares. A BLS seasonal quirk from the missing 2025 data adds 5bp to October's reading, per Goldman, putting its underlying core near 0.11%. Goldman's own caveat is upside oil risk. The report adds a second: core PCE will not get the same relief, since the health insurance reset does not reach it, and household inflation expectations and PPI are both running hotter.
